newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber-Japan prices likely to keep falling.
newsitem.headline: Rubber-Japan prices likely to keep falling.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures are expected to keep sliding, with no clear floor in sight, due to signs of poor-quality rubber coming to market, traders said on Friday.

"Even after sharp price falls this week, rubber prices still have more room to dip. The TOCOM benchmark December rubber may probe the 116.0 yen level early next week," one analyst at a commodity brokerage said.
Market sentiment was battered this week after the spot June contract expired on Tuesday at lower-than-expected levels as market players were wary of accepting deliveries due to concerns over quality.

"Market players believe that there will be larger amounts of poor-quality rubber delivered at the July spot expiry. That factor helped accelerate the downward slide for most of this week," the analyst said.
The benchmark December contract on the Tokyo Commodities Exchange (TOCOM) ended the morning session at 122.4 yen per kg on Friday, against 121.3 yen on Thursday.
Similarly, the benchmark December on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was quoted at 121.4 yen against 121.0 yen on Thursday.

Talk that the Thai government would intervene in the market to prop up Ribbed Smoked Sheet (RSS) 3 grade prices has prompted producers to manufacture that grade even when the quality did not meet the RSS 3 criteria, traders said.
Some traders said that buying was likely to emerge if prices drop much further.
"Although bearish sentiment in Japanese rubber prices is intact, bargain-hunting buying may take place once the market has bottomed out," another analyst at a commodity broker said.
Thai rubber to Japan was offered at 105.00 U.S. cents per kg on an FOB basis on Friday, down from 113.00 U.S. cents on June 20.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users was quoted at 128 yen per kg as of Friday, compared with 143 yen a week ago.
